evidence: Supplied PULSE statement/action forms and authored offline clock/scheduler tests; no hardware output or native timing execution

sources.topic: PULSE DOUT statement/action, NOWAIT, eight-millisecond rounding, zero/range limits and pause/abort behavior

implemented.syntax: INTEGER DOUT port and duration expressions, optional NOWAIT on statements only; automatic cooperative generation and transitive blocking delay effects
implemented.duration: Zero no-op, positive duration rounded upward to eight milliseconds, maximum 86400000; deterministic rounded expiry rather than native scan jitter
implemented.execution: Existing blocking DELAY driver or pending NOWAIT output; explicit captured host clock or scheduler virtual time
implemented.ownership: Root-caller ownership through linked routines, independent output deadlines, pause/completion expiry, terminal freeze and successful-write cancellation
implemented.observation: Source-located value-free records, explicit polling, port read/snapshot and checkpoint servicing; pending work excluded from JSON restore

portable_choices: A standalone blocking sleep callback completes the modeled delay on return; it need not advance a host clock
Scheduled pulses always use scheduler virtual time; scheduler run drains pulse deadlines after completion or pause and can jump idle time
Overlapping pulses reject until expiry or an explicit write cancels the previous deadline
Successful source/indirect/host writes take ownership; failed writes leave pending work intact
Abort/STOP/failure freeze the last modeled value and discard pending work on polling; no terminal cleanup drives an output off
Host polling is explicit and no background threads run; clock samples validate as a batch before expiration changes
Snapshots preserve observed values only, so a restored on value has no inherited deadline
remaining: Physical output adapters, native port modes, scan jitter, controller timing/lifecycle acceptance and strict mode
